description: Consistency audit of the path-integrated potential scale using the thin-lens relation int|Phi|dl = (c^2/2) D_Delta psi.
classification: GR potential-delay diagnostic; not an additional conformal TEP prediction
conformal_cancellation_reason: For B=0, g_tilde=A^2 g has the same null curves as g. The static psi-dependent Shapiro/Fermat delay is already included in the GR lens prediction.

map_normalisation_reconciliation.archive_convention: GLAFIC v3 maps scaled to D_ls/D_s = 1 (z_s -> infinity; HLSP readme)
map_normalisation_reconciliation.interpretation: At the published image positions the map/table ratio is uniform to ~3%, identifying the documented D_ls/D_s = 1 normalisation (expected factor 1/beta = 1.873, measured 1.867). The earlier ~4x non-uniform mismatch was caused by erroneous image positions ~10 arcsec north of the image field, not a map defect.

sign_check.psi_ordering_meaning: radial: psi is a bowl with its minimum at the cluster centre; smallest psi = smallest cluster-centric radius (SX ~9.3 arcsec vs 12-14 arcsec for S1-S4)

local_depth_ordering.interpretation: TEP field tracks the local potential/density (same Poisson source); SX samples the deepest temporal environment and is predicted to arrive latest

sign_check.evidential_status: ordering diagnostic only; GR potential already subtracted

centre.note: psi-map minimum (potential centre), not the WCS reference pixel

smooth_deprojection_crosscheck.limitation: Azimuthally averaged spherical deprojection retains only the cluster monopole and misses the member-galaxy sub-structure around S1-S4 and the near-critical compression at SX; the full-2D rescaled kappa map is the primary local-density diagnostic.  Neither ordering is an additional static conformal propagation prediction.

bugs_fixed_relative_to_step_50_51: step_50 applied the endpoint clock ratio Gamma(Phi_i) to delay differences; that quantity is not a propagation residual.
step_51 ray geometry used r = sqrt(b^2 + (s*angle)^2) with angle ~ 1e-4, so the cluster potential never truncated over the ~5 Gpc path (~4400x inflation).
step_51 divided dl [Mpc] by c [km/s], missing the 3.086e19 km/Mpc conversion; the resulting t_TEP was never used in the residual.

step_56 previously counted the GR Shapiro/Fermat potential a second time as an additional conformal TEP delay; conformal null-curve invariance makes that additional static contribution identically zero.

steps 50/51/56/054 sampled the GLAFIC maps at incorrect image positions ~10 arcsec north of the published coordinates (Dec ~22.398 instead of ~22.396), inside the cluster core; corrected positions recover the documented D_ls/D_s = 1 map normalisation (uniform 1.878 map/table ratio = 1/beta(1.489) = 1.873) and show psi_SX is the smallest, not largest, of the five.
verdict: The GLAFIC psi map gives the ordinary path-integrated potential scale. At the published image positions, psi_SX = 1136.5 arcsec^2 is the SMALLEST of the five images: the deflection potential is a bowl with its minimum at the cluster centre, so the psi ordering is a cluster-centric radius ordering (SX at ~9.3 arcsec, S1-S4 at 12-14 arcsec), not a local temporal-field-depth ordering.  The TEP field tracks the local potential and projected density (same Poisson source): by those measures SX samples the deepest environment of the five (rescaled kappa_SX = 0.968, the maximum; deprojected local |Phi| ordering: ['SX', 'S2', 'S1', 'S3', 'S4']), so SX arriving latest is the sign the mechanism predicts -- matching the observed +30.1 d residual direction.  This is an environment ordering only: the corresponding Shapiro/Fermat term is already inside every GR lens prediction, and a static conformal factor preserves null curves exactly, so the additional conformal propagation residual is zero. Fitting an extra psi template to +30.1 d would require alpha = -0.0052 (sign-flipped and suppressed relative to |kappa_lens| by a factor 0.09); it is calibrated on the same residual and has no first-principles status.  A non-zero TEP amplitude must be obtained from scalar backreaction, time dependence, or the disformal sector without double-counting the GR Fermat potential.
